name: rosetta-special-characters
code:
use IO.Std.write_line

escape(written: string, produced: char) =>
    write_line("{written,-10} U+{cast int(produced):X4}")

write_line("escape     character")

escape("\\t", '\t')
escape("\\n", '\n')
escape("\\r", '\r')
escape("\\\\", '\\')
escape("\\\"", '\"')
escape("\\u20AC", '€')

write_line("")
write_line("a brace in an interpolated string is doubled: {{ }}")

let `class = "a keyword is an identifier behind a backtick"
write_line(`class)

write_line("a backtick ends the digits of a literal: {0x20AC`c}")
fullSource:
use IO.Std.write_line

escape(written: string, produced: char) =>
    write_line("{written,-10} U+{cast int(produced):X4}")

write_line("escape     character")

escape("\\t", '\t')
escape("\\n", '\n')
escape("\\r", '\r')
escape("\\\\", '\\')
escape("\\\"", '\"')
escape("\\u20AC", '€')

write_line("")
write_line("a brace in an interpolated string is doubled: {{ }}")

let `class = "a keyword is an identifier behind a backtick"
write_line(`class)

write_line("a backtick ends the digits of a literal: {0x20AC`c}")
output:
escape     character
\t         U+0009
\n         U+000A
\r         U+000D
\\         U+005C
\"         U+0022
\u20AC     U+20AC

a brace in an interpolated string is doubled: { }
a keyword is an identifier behind a backtick
a backtick ends the digits of a literal: €
